hints.title: Independent Component Quantization
hints.text: The total squared color similarity error decomposes into the sum of three independent squared errors across red, green, and blue channels.

hints.title: Nearest Multiple of 17 Rounding
hints.text: Shorthand hex colors have equal repeated digits (00, 11, ..., ff), representing multiples of 17 in base 10 (0 * 17 = 0, 1 * 17 = 17, ..., 15 * 17 = 255).

hints.title: Channel Quantization Blueprint
hints.text: For each 2-character hex slice: convert to int decimal value V. Compute round(V / 17). Convert this quotient into a single hex digit and double it.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def similarRGB(self, color: str) -> str:
        def round_channel(hex_str):
            val = int(hex_str, 16)
            idx = round(val / 17)
            return f"{idx:x}{idx:x}"

        r = round_channel(color[1:3])
        g = round_channel(color[3:5])
        b = round_channel(color[5:7])
        return f"#{r}{g}{b}"
```

complexity.notes: Three channel roundings each execute in constant mathematical operations.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Searching all 16^3 = 4096 shorthand colors is unnecessary when each channel is independent.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Constant time modular rounding requires zero heap allocation.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Recognizing 0x11 = 17 decimal property of repeated hex characters.

solutions.approach: C++ Channel Rounding via Division by 17
